scope: Primary literature and official publication records relevant to long-range O(N) criticality, functional renormalization group calculations, the long-range/short-range crossover, and the bibliography of arXiv:2602.07818v2.

verification_policy.bibliographic_metadata: Checked against an official journal record or the current arXiv record. No metadata inferred from secondary summaries is included.
verification_policy.claims: Each allowed_claim is deliberately narrower than the paper's full conclusions and may be cited in the report only for the stated purpose.
verification_policy.preprints: An arXiv DOI is not treated as evidence of peer review. Preprints without a verified journal record have peer_reviewed=false.
verification_policy.numerical_values: Values are transcribed from the cited paper's table or from exact short-range results; parenthetical digits are the uncertainty quoted by the source.

references.title: The 4-ε Expansion for Long-range Interacting Systems
allowed_claims: The v2 manuscript claims a two-loop correction to η beyond 2-σ and argues for a crossover at σ*=2.
The manuscript uses a finite-momentum subtraction with a derivative with respect to |q|^σ while not independently renormalizing the local q² operator.
The discussion explicitly leaves simultaneous renormalization of the short-range operator K_s(-Δ) as future work.

references.title: Critical Exponents for Long-Range Interactions
allowed_claims: Introduces the perturbative expansion controlled by ε'=2σ-d for long-range O(N) models.
Finds η=2-σ through the calculated second order and conjectures that this relation is exact in the long-range regime.
Provides the standard leading perturbative results near the long-range upper critical dimension d=2σ.

references.title: Recursion Relations and Fixed Points for Ferromagnets with Long-Range Interactions
allowed_claims: Original source of the crossover criterion σ*=2-η_SR.
Supports treating the long-range interaction as a perturbation whose stability must be evaluated at the interacting short-range fixed point.

references.title: Crossover between field theories with short-range and long-range exchange or correlations
references.venue: Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and General 22, 751–763
allowed_claims: Gives an all-orders perturbative analysis of the crossover between long-range and short-range field theories.
Supports the continuity and fixed-point stability structure underlying the Sak crossover criterion.

references.title: Fixed-point structure and effective fractional dimensionality for O(N) models with long-range interactions
allowed_claims: Provides a nonperturbative functional renormalization group treatment of long-range O(N) models.
In a truncation containing both Z_σ q^σ and Z_2 q², obtains no flow of the nonanalytic Z_σ term while the analytic Z_2 term flows.
Finds that the long-range fixed point branches from or merges with the short-range fixed point at σ*=2-η_SR.
Introduces an effective-dimension correspondence in LPA and LPA', but that correspondence is an approximation and not an exact identity for interacting fixed points.

references.title: Universality in long-range interacting systems: The effective dimension approach
allowed_claims: Reviews and extends the effective-dimension approach using functional RG methods.
States that the effective-dimension mapping is approximate at non-Gaussian fixed points and reports typical agreement above 97% in the comparisons performed.
May support a quantitative comparison between an FRG approximation and bootstrap data, but not a claim that the mapping is exact.

references.title: Conformal Invariance in the Long-Range Ising Model
allowed_claims: Proves conformal invariance of the long-range Ising fixed point to all orders in the long-range ε expansion by embedding it as a defect theory.
Supports the nonlocal continuum description and the special conformal structure of the long-range fixed point.

references.title: Long-Range Critical Exponents near the Short-Range Crossover
allowed_claims: Provides a weakly coupled description of long-range critical exponents near the short-range crossover.
Supports a continuous crossover at σ*=2-η_SR and the protected long-range field dimension Δ_φ=(d-σ)/2.

references.title: A scaling theory for the long-range to short-range crossover and an infrared duality
references.venue: Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and Theoretical 50, 354002
allowed_claims: Develops the detailed scaling theory and infrared duality for the long-range/short-range crossover.
Gives Δ_φ=(d-σ)/2 on the long-range branch and σ*=2-η_SR.
Explains the crossover using the short-range fixed point coupled to an additional Gaussian field and discusses logarithmic corrections at the crossover.

references.title: Analytic and numerical bootstrap for the long-range Ising model
allowed_claims: Combines analytic and numerical conformal bootstrap for the long-range Ising model in two and three dimensions.
Uses the exact protected dimension Δ_φ=(d-σ)/2 and exact operator-product relations following from the local higher-dimensional description.
The current arXiv version incorporates the corrected three-loop input from arXiv:2411.00805.

references.title: Critical Two-Point Function for Long-Range O(n) Models Below the Upper Critical Dimension
allowed_claims: Provides a rigorous renormalization-group proof near the long-range upper critical dimension that the critical two-point function decays as r^{-(d-α)} for the stated weak-coupling regime.
Supports exact sticking of the long-range two-point exponent in the theorem's stated domain; it should not be cited as a theorem for every dimension, coupling, or crossover point.

references.title: Long-range multi-scalar models at three loops
references.venue: Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and Theoretical 53, 445008
allowed_claims: Computes three-loop beta functions and critical exponents for long-range quartic multi-scalar models at fixed dimension using ε'=2σ-d.
Supports the standard renormalization organization in which the nonlocal kinetic term is protected.
Any numerical three-loop value must be taken together with the 2025 addendum that corrects one diagram.

references.title: Addendum: Long-range multi-scalar models at three loops
references.venue: Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and Theoretical 58, 129401
allowed_claims: Corrects one Feynman diagram in the 2020 three-loop beta functions and supplies updated numerical critical exponents.
Must be cited whenever corrected three-loop numerical data from the 2020 calculation are used.

references.title: Convergence of Nonperturbative Approximations to the Renormalization Group
allowed_claims: Provides analytical arguments and a three-dimensional Ising test supporting convergence of the derivative expansion for well-behaved regulators.
Studies the derivative expansion through order six and gives regulator-selection and error-estimation guidance.
Provides the O(∂⁶) three-dimensional Ising estimates later tabulated as ν=0.63012(16) and η=0.0361(11) by De Polsi et al.
Does not directly establish convergence rates for the nonanalytic long-range two-kinetic-operator truncation.

references.title: Precision calculation of critical exponents in the O(N) universality classes with the nonperturbative renormalization group
allowed_claims: Computes ν, η, and ω for short-range O(N) universality classes with the nonperturbative RG derivative expansion through O(∂⁴).
Its N=1 comparison table separately transcribes the earlier Balog et al. O(∂⁶) estimates ν=0.63012(16), η=0.0361(11) and the Kos et al. conformal-bootstrap benchmark.
Reports apparent order-by-order convergence with an empirical small parameter typically between 1/9 and 1/4 and supplies error bars.
May be used to motivate higher derivative orders and systematic truncation estimates, but it is not itself a long-range O(N) FRG calculation.

references.title: Defects in the long-range O(N) model
references.venue: Journal of Physics A: Mathematical and Theoretical 58, 335401
allowed_claims: For the bulk long-range O(N) model, states that the nonlocal field does not renormalize because renormalization introduces local counterterms.
Describes a near-four-dimensional expansion with an additional parameter as treating nonlocality as a perturbation of the local four-dimensional theory.
Introduces and studies three constructions of conformal defects; it is not a bulk FRG computation.

references.title: Critical exponent η of isotropic spin systems with long and short-range interactions
allowed_claims: Discusses η and stability in weakly long-range, intermediate-range, and long-range regimes for isotropic N-component spin systems.
May be cited as an early competing field-theory analysis, with its approximation and historical context stated explicitly.

references.title: The Boundary between Long-Range and Short-Range Critical Behavior
allowed_claims: Monte Carlo study of the two-dimensional long-range Ising model finding the crossover at interaction decay r^{-15/4}.
For the convention J(r)∼r^{-(d+σ)} with d=2, this corresponds to σ*=7/4 and supports Sak's criterion.

references.title: Critical behavior of the Ising model with long range interactions
allowed_claims: Reports two-dimensional long-range Ising Monte Carlo results near the intermediate-to-short-range changeover that the author interprets as disagreement with the standard RG prediction.
The official arXiv record does not list a journal publication DOI; it must not be cited with 10.1103/PhysRevLett.28.240.

references.title: Relations between Short Range and Long Range Ising models
allowed_claims: Finds that a subdominant second power law produces strong corrections in two-dimensional long-range Ising correlations near the crossover.
After including that correction, reports numerical data consistent with Sak's prediction.

references.title: On Sak's criterion for statistical models with long-range interaction
allowed_claims: Reports large-scale Monte Carlo simulations up to L=8192 for the two-dimensional long-range Ising model.
The authors interpret their critical polynomial, Binder ratio, η, and 1/ν data as evidence for σ*=2 rather than Sak's σ*=7/4.
This result is a recent non-peer-reviewed counterclaim and must be presented as disputed, not as established consensus.

references.title: The Nonclassical Regime of the Two-dimensional Long-range XY Model: A Comprehensive Monte Carlo Study
allowed_claims: Reports Monte Carlo evidence for a single second-order transition into a long-range-ordered phase for σ≤2 in the two-dimensional long-range XY model.
Reports the Table 5 estimates of y_t=1/ν and η transcribed below and interprets them as supporting σ*=2.
Does not by itself settle the vortex-sector controversy; it should be discussed together with RG work that includes spin-wave/vortex coupling.

references.title: Two-Dimensional XY Ferromagnet Induced by Long-Range Interaction
allowed_claims: Reports large-scale Monte Carlo evidence for long-range order for σ<2 and logarithmic behavior at σ=2 in the two-dimensional long-range XY model.
May be cited as a separate shorter XY study; it is not the same publication as Physical Review B 112, 144429.

references.title: Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking in Two-dimensional Long-range Heisenberg Model
allowed_claims: Reports two-dimensional long-range Heisenberg Monte Carlo simulations up to L=8192 and a continuous finite-temperature transition into a long-range-ordered phase for σ≤2.
The authors interpret the results as a crossover at σ*=2 and report the Table 1 exponent estimates transcribed below.
This is a non-peer-reviewed preprint; the current v2 author list differs from the stale entry in the target manuscript.

references.title: Persistence of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless Transition with Long-Range Couplings
allowed_claims: Uses Landau-Peierls arguments and higher-order RG including spin-wave/topological-excitation coupling.
Finds no direct magnetized-to-disordered transition and concludes that the BKT transition persists for arbitrary long-range exponents.
Provides a published result directly conflicting with the recent single-transition XY Monte Carlo interpretation, demonstrating that the XY phase diagram remains actively disputed.

references.title: Bootstrapping Mixed Correlators in the 3D Ising Model
allowed_claims: Primary conformal-bootstrap source for the three-dimensional Ising scaling-dimension benchmark transcribed by De Polsi et al.
The benchmark values may be converted to eta and nu using the standard three-dimensional scaling-dimension relations.

references.title: Spin-spin correlation functions for the two-dimensional Ising model: Exact theory in the scaling region
allowed_claims: Provides the exact two-dimensional Ising spin-correlation functions and their scaling-region asymptotics.
Supports the standard exact short-range Ising benchmark eta=1/4 and correlation-length scaling nu=1 used only as a diagnostic comparison.

d2_short_range_exact.use: Exact benchmark for the stability eigenvalue of a long-range perturbation at the two-dimensional short-range Ising fixed point.

At the BKT transition the correlation length has an essential, not power-law, divergence; a finite Wilson-Fisher ν must not be assigned. A smooth-potential FRG without vortex fugacity is not a complete benchmark for this case.

The two-dimensional short-range classical Heisenberg model has no ordinary finite-temperature critical fixed point, so Sak's formula cannot be evaluated by inserting conventional finite-T η_SR and ν_SR values.

recent_d2_ising_counterclaim.interpretation_limit: These are the preprint authors' finite-size-scaling estimates. They are evidence in an active controversy, not exact values and not a substitute for an operator-resolved field-theory calculation.

d2_xy_monte_carlo.interpretation_limit: The table is a benchmark for the published Monte Carlo fit, but the claimed one-transition topology is disputed by walther_willsher_knolle_2026, which includes vortex/spin-wave coupling.

d2_heisenberg_preprint.interpretation_limit: These values are copied from arXiv:2512.01956v2 Table 1 and remain non-peer-reviewed.

report_guardrails: Do not describe σ*=2-η_SR as supported only by historical consensus: cite the operator-stability argument, nonperturbative FRG, all-orders perturbation theory, CFT, and the rigorous theorem within each source's domain.

Do not describe the recent σ*=2 Monte Carlo interpretation as settled. The two-dimensional Ising and Heisenberg results are preprints, and the XY transition topology has a directly conflicting peer-reviewed RG analysis.
Do not use De Polsi et al. 2020 as if it were a long-range FRG paper. It supports the high-order derivative-expansion methodology and error-budget strategy only.
Do not quote uncorrected numerical values from Benedetti et al. 2020 without the 2025 addendum.
At σ=2 the q^σ and q² operators become degenerate; results at that marginal point require a two-operator and logarithmic-crossover analysis rather than extrapolation of a single kinetic term.
